reader.requirement: After an explicit or implicit CANCEL of a program, the only event that re-establishes a logical relationship between the run unit and that program is a later CALL statement naming it: a CALL of another program, a repeated CANCEL, or a re-call of the program's container must not re-establish it, and the next CALL naming it finds it in its initial state and then in last-used state on later calls.

reader.notes: CallProgram is the only member that sets CalledSinceCancel and creates a cached instance; CancelNode clears both and resets statics, and cascades to contained programs in reverse order. No other runtime path re-instantiates a cancelled program, so only a CALL naming it re-establishes it.

refuter.evidence: r6x.cob at --std 85: X1 Y1 Y2 / X2 Z Y1 Y2 / X3 Y1 / I1 IY1 OPEN 00 / I1 IY1 OPEN 00 / SA1 / SA1 / SA2. That covers what the reader did not try. (1) An explicit CANCEL of a COMMON contained program Y by its container X, on a later activation of X that was not cancelled: the sibling Z's CALL naming Y re-establishes Y in its initial state. (2) A double CANCEL Y is no action, and the next CALL finds Y initial. (3) The implicit cancel of an INITIAL program cascades to its contained IY: IY is initial again and its internal file was closed (GR4, GR10), so a second OPEN OUTPUT gives 00. (4) CANCEL and CALL by an identifier holding a space-padded name, with the re-establishing CALL in the 85 ON OVERFLOW form: OVERFLOW is not taken, SA restarts at 1, then last-used (SA2). Grep of Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect over ProgramTable.cs: only the GR5 flag the reader named. cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.3.4 GR6; OK §1985:X.5.3.4 GR4.
